authors: Xavier Gabaix, Ralph S. J. Koijen, Robert J. Richmond, Motohiro Yogo
title: Asset Embeddings
why_it_matters: Core paper for reverse-engineering institutional decision logic from holdings. It reframes assets and investors as objects with learned latent positions, which is directly relevant to inferring demand, substitution, and investor-specific preference structure.
abstract_summary: Uses portfolio holdings to learn asset representations and connect those embeddings to demand, substitution, and equilibrium asset-pricing behavior.

authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen, Motohiro Yogo
title: A Demand System Approach to Asset Pricing
venue: Journal of Political Economy / NBER Working Paper 21749
why_it_matters: Load-bearing framework: it converts investor holdings into estimable demand curves. This is the cleanest academic bridge between observed portfolio positions and latent decision logic.
abstract_summary: Builds an asset-pricing demand system using investor-level portfolio holdings and market clearing to estimate elasticities and pricing effects.

authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen, Motohiro Yogo
title: On the Theory and Econometrics of (Demand System) Asset Pricing
why_it_matters: This is the technical econometrics companion to demand-system asset pricing. Read after Koijen-Yogo 2019 to understand identification, estimation, and failure modes.
abstract_summary: Develops theoretical and econometric foundations for demand-system asset-pricing estimation.

authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen, Robert J. Richmond, Motohiro Yogo
title: Which Investors Matter for Equity Valuations and Expected Returns?
why_it_matters: Directly addresses which investor classes move prices. For a founder building trader-decision reverse engineering, this tells you whose decisions are worth modeling first.
abstract_summary: Studies how investor heterogeneity maps into valuations and expected returns.
access_note: OUP/institutional access likely required; search author pages for preprint.

authors: Maarten P. Scholl, Mahmoud Mahfouz, Anisoara Calinescu, J. Doyne Farmer
title: Learning to Manage Investment Portfolios beyond Simple Utility Functions
why_it_matters: Important because it questions the simple utility-function assumption behind many portfolio models. It fits the thesis that real investors optimize messy, multi-objective, path-dependent decision rules.
abstract_summary: Uses learning-based portfolio-management methods to move beyond fixed mean-variance or simple utility objectives.

authors: Miguel Anton, Lauren Cohen, Christopher Polk
title: Best Ideas
venue: SSRN / Harvard Business School Working Paper 21-004
why_it_matters: Useful for extracting manager conviction from portfolio concentration. It is a practical bridge between 13F holdings and trade selection logic.
abstract_summary: Examines whether concentrated portfolio positions reveal managers' highest-conviction investment ideas.

authors: Daniel Angelini, Hamish Iqbal, Farouk Jivraj
title: Systematic 13F Hedge Fund Alpha
why_it_matters: Applied 13F alpha paper. Treat it as a practical benchmark for what can be inferred from public institutional holdings without overbuilding a fantasy model.
abstract_summary: Tests systematic strategies derived from hedge-fund 13F filings and portfolio disclosures.

authors: Bryan T. Kelly, Boris Kuznetsov, Semyon Malamud, Teng Andrea Xu
title: Artificial Intelligence Asset Pricing Models
why_it_matters: Frontier ML asset-pricing work. Useful as a benchmark for when an AI model is genuinely pricing risk versus curve-fitting alpha labels.
abstract_summary: Applies transformer-based AI models to stochastic discount factor estimation and compares pricing-error reductions to classical methods.

authors: Xavier Gabaix, Ralph S. J. Koijen
title: In Search of the Origins of Financial Fluctuations: The Inelastic Markets Hypothesis
venue: Quarterly Journal of Economics / NBER Working Paper 28967
why_it_matters: Explains why flows can have large price impact. This is the economic reason investor-decision inference matters: demand shocks do not get harmlessly absorbed in perfectly elastic markets.
abstract_summary: Argues that aggregate demand shifts can move prices strongly when market demand curves are inelastic.

authors: Igor Halperin, Petter Kolm, Gordon Ritter
title: RL and IRL: A Practitioner's Guide for Investment Management
venue: CFA Institute Research Foundation, AI in Asset Management, Chapter 6
why_it_matters: High-signal practitioner bridge from RL theory to investment use cases. Use it to avoid academic RL toy problems that do not survive execution costs and portfolio constraints.
abstract_summary: Surveys reinforcement learning and inverse reinforcement learning for investment-management workflows.
access_note: CFA chapter landing/source should be checked for PDF availability.

title: QLBS Q-Learner Goes NuQLear: Fitted Q Iteration, Inverse RL, and Option Pricing
why_it_matters: Shows how option pricing, hedging, and RL can be put in the same control framework. Good bridge from mathematical finance to RL implementation.
abstract_summary: Extends the QLBS framework using fitted Q-iteration and inverse-RL ideas for derivatives and hedging.

title: G-Learner and GIRL: Goal-Based Wealth Management with Reinforcement Learning and Inverse Reinforcement Learning
why_it_matters: One of the clearest finance-specific IRL papers. It targets investor objective inference rather than only return prediction.
abstract_summary: Applies RL and IRL to infer and optimize goal-based wealth-management objectives.

authors: Jacobo Roa-Vicens, Cyrine Chtourou, Angelos Filos, Francisco Rullan, Yarin Gal, Ricardo Silva
title: Towards Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Limit Order Book Dynamics
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to recovering agent objectives from order-book behavior. It is more aligned with execution/microstructure than portfolio-level utility inference.
abstract_summary: Explores how IRL can infer latent objectives underlying limit-order-book dynamics.

title: Bayesian and Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Limit Order Book Simulators
why_it_matters: Thesis-length treatment of LOB simulators and IRL. Useful if the product goal is not just predicting prices, but simulating trader populations.
abstract_summary: Develops Bayesian and adversarial IRL approaches for building limit-order-book simulators.
access_note: Locate exact UCL thesis record before download.

authors: Jon Hendricks, Daniel Harmon, Umut Demirel, Chang Yun, Daniel P. Sanderson, Douglas L. T. Rohde
title: Inferring Agent Objectives at Different Scales of a Complex System
why_it_matters: Useful for multi-scale objective inference. Trading systems have micro-objectives at order level and macro-objectives at portfolio level; this paper frames that scale problem.
abstract_summary: Studies inference of latent agent objectives across multiple scales in complex systems.

authors: Sinong Geng, Houssam Nassif, Carlos Manzanares, Andrew Jaegle, Samy Bengio
title: Deep PQR: Solving Inverse Reinforcement Learning using Anchor Actions
why_it_matters: Not finance-specific, but useful when demonstrations are sparse or ambiguous. Anchor-action structure maps well to constrained action spaces in execution and rebalancing.
abstract_summary: Presents an IRL method using anchor actions to recover rewards in complex environments.

title: Heuristic-Guided Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Portfolio Optimization
why_it_matters: Potentially high-signal if the final paper is accessible. It directly targets portfolio optimization with IRL, but the exact free PDF should be verified before relying on it.
abstract_summary: Applies heuristic guidance to IRL for portfolio-allocation problems.
access_note: Verify final IJCAI paper page and authors before citation use.

title: Transaction-Aware Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Trading in Stock Markets
why_it_matters: Relevant because it uses transaction-aware constraints rather than idealized state/action loops. Needs institutional access or author manuscript.
abstract_summary: Studies IRL methods for stock-trading decisions while accounting for transaction structure.

title: Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
why_it_matters: The foundation. It defines the original IRL problem: infer the reward function that explains observed expert behavior.
abstract_summary: Introduces algorithms for recovering reward functions from expert demonstrations.

title: Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
why_it_matters: Important for imitation from demonstrations. The closest analogue in finance is learning from expert trade trajectories or manager holdings.
abstract_summary: Shows how to learn policies from expert demonstrations by matching feature expectations.

authors: Brian D. Ziebart, Andrew L. Maas, J. Andrew Bagnell, Anind K. Dey
title: Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning
why_it_matters: Critical because it handles non-unique explanations of behavior by preferring maximum-entropy distributions. Finance needs this because multiple motives can explain the same trade.
abstract_summary: Introduces maximum-entropy formulation for probabilistic reward inference from demonstrations.

title: Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning
why_it_matters: A natural fit for markets because reward inference should carry uncertainty. Useful for avoiding overconfident claims about an investor's objective.
abstract_summary: Uses Bayesian inference to estimate posterior distributions over reward functions.

title: Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning
why_it_matters: The modern imitation-learning anchor. It connects adversarial learning with occupancy-measure matching, useful for trade-sequence imitation.
abstract_summary: Formulates imitation learning as adversarial training between policy and discriminator.

authors: Stephane Ross, Geoffrey Gordon, Drew Bagnell
title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
why_it_matters: DAgger addresses compounding errors from pure behavioral cloning. In trading agents, small early errors compound into very different positions and exposure.
abstract_summary: Introduces Dataset Aggregation for robust imitation learning under distribution shift.

authors: Chelsea Finn, Sergey Levine, Pieter Abbeel
title: Guided Cost Learning: Deep Inverse Optimal Control via Policy Optimization
why_it_matters: Useful for high-dimensional reward learning when the cost function is unknown. Good conceptual link to inferring non-linear investor objectives.
abstract_summary: Combines cost learning with policy optimization for inverse optimal control.

authors: Justin Fu, Katie Luo, Sergey Levine
title: Learning Robust Rewards with Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning
why_it_matters: AIRL separates reward recovery from policy imitation more cleanly than vanilla GAIL. That matters if the goal is to infer decision logic, not merely copy behavior.
abstract_summary: Introduces adversarial inverse reinforcement learning with more transferable recovered rewards.

authors: Florian Tramer, Fan Zhang, Ari Juels, Michael K. Reiter, Thomas Ristenpart
title: Stealing Machine Learning Models via Prediction APIs
why_it_matters: Foundational model-extraction paper. Relevant as a conceptual analogue to reverse-engineering decision policies from external observable behavior.
abstract_summary: Shows how prediction APIs can leak enough information to reconstruct model behavior.

authors: Nicolas Papernot, Patrick McDaniel, Ian Goodfellow, Somesh Jha, Z. Berkay Celik, Ananth Grama
title: Practical Black-Box Attacks against Machine Learning
why_it_matters: Important for black-box query learning. In finance, the equivalent is querying/observing reactions and reconstructing latent policies under limited feedback.
abstract_summary: Develops substitute-model methods for attacking black-box ML systems.

title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model
why_it_matters: Current-generation model-extraction example. It shows that partial extraction of high-capacity systems can be practical under specific leakage channels.
abstract_summary: Demonstrates extraction of part of a production-scale language model under black-box access.

authors: Kalpesh Krishna, Gaurav Singh Tomar, Ankur P. Parikh, Nicolas Papernot, Mohit Iyyer
title: Thieves on Sesame Street! Model Extraction of BERT-based APIs
why_it_matters: Useful for NLP/LLM agent settings. It covers extraction of behavior from black-box text APIs, relevant to competitor-agent monitoring.
abstract_summary: Studies extraction attacks against BERT-based prediction services.

title: Yes, My LoRD: Lower-Dimensional Subspace Discovery for Efficient Model Extraction
why_it_matters: Recent model-extraction work focused on efficiency. Relevant when the observed system is too expensive to query exhaustively.
abstract_summary: Proposes lower-dimensional subspace discovery methods for more efficient model extraction.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
title: Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors
why_it_matters: The baseline empirical paper on individual investor underperformance. Any psychometric or behavior-inference model should understand these behavioral regularities first.
abstract_summary: Analyzes individual investor trading records and finds frequent trading harms performance.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
title: Boys Will Be Boys: Gender, Overconfidence, and Common Stock Investment
why_it_matters: Important because it links overconfidence to trading intensity. This is a practical warning for models that infer skill from activity volume.
abstract_summary: Studies gender-linked overconfidence and turnover in investor trading behavior.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
title: Are Investors Reluctant to Realize Their Losses?
why_it_matters: Disposition-effect anchor. It maps directly into trader decision logic: sell winners, hold losers, and distort realized PnL distributions.
abstract_summary: Tests whether investors disproportionately realize gains and defer realizing losses.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
authors: Cary Frydman, Nicholas Barberis, Colin Camerer, Peter Bossaerts, Antonio Rangel
title: Using Neural Data to Test a Theory of Investor Behavior
why_it_matters: High-signal behavioral bridge from neuroeconomics to trading decisions. Useful for understanding how utility and reference-point theories can be tested biologically.
abstract_summary: Uses neural data to test investor behavior theories around gains, losses, and realization decisions.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
authors: Yanou Ramon, R. A. Farrokhnia, Sandra C. Matz, David Martens
title: Explainable AI for Psychological Profiling from Financial Transaction Records
why_it_matters: Not trading-specific but directly relevant to inferring psychological traits from financial records. Useful for thinking about what can and cannot be inferred from transaction traces.
abstract_summary: Uses explainable machine learning to infer psychological profiles from financial transaction data.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
authors: Nicholas Barberis, Lawrence Jin, Baolian Wang
title: Prospect Theory and Stock Market Anomalies
why_it_matters: Connects prospect theory to asset-pricing anomalies. Useful when translating behavioral decision rules into systematic return predictions.
abstract_summary: Explores how prospect-theory preferences can explain stock-market anomalies.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
authors: Nicola Gennaioli, Yueran Ma, Andrei Shleifer
title: Expectations and Investment
why_it_matters: Useful for expectation formation and macro-investment linkages. It adds a real-economy counterpart to purely market-level behavioral models.
abstract_summary: Studies how expectations shape investment behavior and macro outcomes.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
authors: Pedro Bordalo, Nicola Gennaioli, Rafael La Porta, Andrei Shleifer
title: Diagnostic Expectations and Stock Returns
why_it_matters: Important for modeling investors who over-extrapolate salient information. This is one of the cleaner behavioral explanations for return predictability.
abstract_summary: Applies diagnostic-expectations theory to stock returns and expectation errors.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
title: Narrative Economics
venue: American Economic Review / NBER Working Paper 23075
why_it_matters: Important for news/story-driven flows. It gives a framework for how narratives can propagate and affect economic decisions.
abstract_summary: Develops a research agenda for studying contagious economic narratives and their market/macroeconomic consequences.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
title: Giving Content to Investor Sentiment: The Role of Media in the Stock Market
why_it_matters: Anchor paper for textual sentiment and markets. It is the old-school empirical basis for many LLM-news trading claims.
abstract_summary: Tests whether media pessimism predicts market activity and returns.

group_title: Behavioral Finance & Psychometric Inference from Trades
title: Bridging Personality and Behavior in Financial Trading
why_it_matters: Potentially relevant to psychometric trader inference, but needs bibliographic verification before it should be treated as load-bearing.
abstract_summary: Appears to connect personality measures with observed financial trading behavior.
access_note: Verify authors, DOI, and final version.

authors: Thomas Henning, Siddhartha M. Ojha, Ross Spoon, Jiatong Han, Colin F. Camerer
title: LLM Trading: Analysis of LLM Agent Behavior in Experimental Asset Markets
why_it_matters: Important because it studies LLM agents as market participants, not just text summarizers. Good for evaluating whether LLM decision behavior is stable under trading incentives.
abstract_summary: Analyzes how LLM agents behave in controlled experimental asset markets.

title: Can Large Language Models Trade?
why_it_matters: Directly tests the central hype claim. Use it as an empirical checkpoint before building agentic trading systems around LLM reasoning.
abstract_summary: Evaluates whether LLMs can generate trading-relevant signals or decisions.

authors: Ryuji Hashimoto, Takehiro Takayanagi, Masahiro Suzuki, Kiyoshi Izumi
title: Agent-Based Simulation of a Financial Market with Large Language Model-Based Agents
why_it_matters: Relevant to market simulation with LLM agents. Useful for separating agent believability from actual alpha.
abstract_summary: Builds a financial-market simulation populated by LLM-based agents.

title: Behavioral Consistency Validation for LLM Agents
why_it_matters: Critical for production agent systems: a trading agent that changes behavior under prompt perturbation is not a strategy, it is a liability.
abstract_summary: Proposes methods to validate behavioral consistency in LLM agents.

title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
why_it_matters: Representative multi-agent LLM trading framework. Useful as a competitor/architecture reference, not as proof of profitable execution.
abstract_summary: Presents a multi-agent LLM framework for financial trading analysis and decision-making.

authors: Yang Li, Yangyang Yu, Haohang Li, Zhi Chen, Khaldoun Khashanah
title: TradingGPT: Multi-Agent System with Layered Memory and Distinct Characters for Enhanced Financial Trading Performance
why_it_matters: Early LLM trading-agent architecture with memory and role separation. Useful as a baseline for what agent frameworks usually overclaim.
abstract_summary: Uses a multi-agent LLM system with layered memory for financial trading decisions.

title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design
why_it_matters: Important memory-based LLM trader reference. Good for comparing retrieval/memory against deterministic feature stores.
abstract_summary: Builds a financial trading agent with layered memory mechanisms.

title: Trading-R1: Financial Trading with LLM Reasoning
why_it_matters: Relevant because reasoning-tuned LLMs are being applied to trading. Treat as experimental until execution-cost and live-trading validation are shown.
abstract_summary: Applies reasoning-oriented LLM methods to trading workflows.

title: QuantAgent: Seeking Holy Grail in Trading by Self-Improving Large Language Model
why_it_matters: Useful as a self-improving agent architecture reference. Needs skepticism: self-improvement can easily become overfit backtest search.
abstract_summary: Proposes a self-improving LLM agent for quantitative trading tasks.

title: Automate Strategy Finding with LLM in Quant Investment
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to automated strategy discovery. Pair with backtest-overfitting papers before trusting any generated strategy.
abstract_summary: Uses LLMs to automate parts of quantitative strategy discovery.

title: GPT-Signal: Generative AI for Semi-Automatic Feature Engineering in the Alpha Research Process
why_it_matters: High practical relevance: LLMs may be better at feature ideation than autonomous trading. This is closer to a credible alpha-research workflow.
abstract_summary: Uses GPT-style systems to assist feature engineering in alpha research.

title: Large Language Model Agent in Financial Trading: A Survey
why_it_matters: Useful map of the LLM trading-agent literature. Read after the primary papers to avoid swallowing survey framing uncritically.
abstract_summary: Surveys LLM-agent systems and tasks in financial trading.

title: TraderTalk: Analyzing Large Language Model Behavior in Simulated Financial Markets
why_it_matters: Relevant for observing LLM strategic behavior in simulated markets. Useful for testing whether agent conversations add signal or only narrative.
abstract_summary: Studies LLM behavior and communication in simulated financial markets.

authors: Maria del Rio-Chanona, Marco Pangallo, Cars Hommes
title: Can Generative AI Agents Behave Like Humans? An Evaluation of Generative AI Agents in Generic Decision-Making Tasks
why_it_matters: Needed to test whether LLM agents are valid behavioral stand-ins. Market simulations fail if the agents are not behaviorally calibrated.
abstract_summary: Evaluates generative AI agents on generic human decision-making tasks.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
why_it_matters: The general agent-simulation ancestor for many financial agent ideas. Useful for architecture, not financial validity.
abstract_summary: Introduces memory/reflection/planning agents that simulate believable human behavior.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
title: Learning to Trade via Direct Reinforcement
why_it_matters: Classic direct RL trading paper. Useful historically, but it predates modern execution-cost and overfitting controls.
abstract_summary: Applies direct reinforcement learning to trading policy optimization.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
title: Deep Direct Reinforcement Learning for Financial Signal Representation and Trading
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
why_it_matters: Modern deep-RL trading anchor. Read with skepticism because deep RL can exploit backtest artifacts.
abstract_summary: Uses deep neural networks and reinforcement learning for financial signal representation and trading.
access_note: IEEE access likely required; search arXiv/author preprint.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
authors: Peer Nagy, Jan-Peter Calliess, Stefan Zohren
title: Asynchronous Deep Double Duelling Q-Learning for Trading-Signal Execution in Limit Order Book Markets
why_it_matters: Important because it focuses on execution in LOB markets rather than abstract buy/sell labels. That is closer to real tradability.
abstract_summary: Applies asynchronous double dueling Q-learning to LOB trading-signal execution.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
authors: Yufei Huang, Junyi Zhou, Di Song
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Portfolio Management
why_it_matters: Useful portfolio RL baseline. Read as an implementation reference, not a profitability proof.
abstract_summary: Applies deep reinforcement learning to portfolio management and allocation.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
authors: Zhengyao Jiang, Dixing Xu, Jinjun Liang
title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for the Financial Portfolio Management Problem
why_it_matters: Widely cited RL portfolio framework. Good for understanding the early architecture pattern and its limitations.
abstract_summary: Builds a deep RL framework for portfolio allocation over multiple assets.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
title: Portfolio Management Based on Value Distribution Reinforcement Learning
why_it_matters: Recent distributional-RL portfolio paper. Useful for comparing return-distribution learning against scalar reward maximization.
abstract_summary: Applies value-distribution reinforcement learning to portfolio-management tasks.
access_note: Verify final Frontiers PDF from DOI page.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
title: Reinforcement Learning for Asset and Portfolio Management
why_it_matters: Potentially high-signal practitioner paper, but JPM is usually paywalled. Find working-paper version before treating as accessible.
abstract_summary: Discusses RL methods for asset and portfolio management.
access_note: PM Research/JPM institutional access likely required.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
title: Planning with Diffusion for Flexible Behavior Synthesis
why_it_matters: Not finance-specific, but diffusion planning is relevant for offline policy generation. Could be adapted to execution or portfolio trajectories.
abstract_summary: Introduces diffusion models as trajectory planners for offline RL/control.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
title: Is Conditional Generative Modeling all you need for Decision Making?
why_it_matters: Decision Diffuser is relevant to offline decision making from historical trajectories. Finance application requires strict leakage and regime controls.
abstract_summary: Uses conditional generative modeling for decision-making trajectories.

group_title: Reinforcement Learning for Trading & Portfolio Management
title: Diffusion World Models
why_it_matters: Useful for model-based RL concepts. For markets, the danger is learning a beautiful world model of stale regimes.
abstract_summary: Combines diffusion modeling with world-model approaches for decision making.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
authors: David Easley, Marcos Lopez de Prado, Maureen O'Hara, Zhibai Zhang
title: Microstructure in the Machine Age
why_it_matters: Important for how machine trading changes market microstructure. This is a better anchor than retail smart-money terminology.
abstract_summary: Studies market microstructure in an era of algorithmic and machine-based trading.
access_note: OUP/institutional access likely required; author preprints may exist.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
authors: Rama Cont, Sasha Stoikov, Rishi Talreja
title: A Stochastic Model for Order Book Dynamics
why_it_matters: Core LOB dynamics model. Useful for simulating queue behavior and understanding why simple candle patterns are lossy.
abstract_summary: Models limit-order-book dynamics using stochastic processes.
access_note: INFORMS access likely required; preprints may exist.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
authors: Álvaro Cartea, Sebastian Jaimungal, José Penalva
title: Algorithmic and High-Frequency Trading
why_it_matters: Best structured book bridge from theory to execution. Use it for market making, optimal execution, and inventory control mechanics.
abstract_summary: Textbook covering execution, market making, and high-frequency trading models.
access_note: Book purchase/institutional access; sample chapters only.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
title: High-Frequency Trading in a Limit Order Book
why_it_matters: Market-making anchor. It formalizes reservation price and inventory-aware quotes, which are still the conceptual base for many market-making systems.
abstract_summary: Develops an inventory-aware optimal market-making model in a limit order book.
access_note: Taylor & Francis access likely required; author preprint often available online.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
title: Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions
why_it_matters: Optimal-execution foundation. Mandatory reading before any strategy claiming edge from trading signals without accounting for implementation shortfall.
abstract_summary: Develops mean-variance optimal execution under market impact and risk trade-offs.
access_note: Direct PDF availability varies by mirror/author source; validate before download.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
title: The Financial Mathematics of Market Liquidity
why_it_matters: Useful for liquidity, inventory, and execution mathematics. Treat as deep background for execution algorithms.
abstract_summary: Textbook on liquidity, market making, and mathematical models of trading costs.
access_note: Book purchase/institutional access; sample chapters only.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
authors: Rama Cont, Arseniy Kukanov, Sasha Stoikov
title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
why_it_matters: Load-bearing microstructure paper. It quantifies order-flow imbalance and price impact better than retail concepts like fair value gaps.
abstract_summary: Studies how order-book events and order-flow imbalance affect price changes.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
title: High-frequency market-making with inventory constraints and directional bets
why_it_matters: Useful extension of market-making models. Connects inventory constraints with directional views.
abstract_summary: Studies high-frequency market making with inventory risk and directional expectations.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
title: How to Correctly Apply Bellman Equation to Avellaneda-Stoikov Market-Making Model
why_it_matters: Recent correction/critique around a widely used market-making model. Useful because many implementations copy formulas without checking assumptions.
abstract_summary: Revisits the Bellman-equation treatment of the Avellaneda-Stoikov model.

group_title: Market Microstructure, Limit Order Books, Execution Algorithms
title: Empirical Market Microstructure
why_it_matters: Important empirical microstructure book. Use it to build sane features around trades, quotes, spreads, and price discovery.
abstract_summary: Textbook treatment of empirical methods for market microstructure.
access_note: Book purchase/institutional access; sample chapters only.

group_title: Quant Foundations - Renaissance / Simons / Medallion lineage
title: The Man Who Solved the Market: How Jim Simons Launched the Quant Revolution
why_it_matters: Not a technical paper, but the best public narrative of Renaissance/Medallion. Useful for understanding culture: data, secrecy, validation, and relentless empirical testing.
abstract_summary: Book-length account of Jim Simons, Renaissance Technologies, and Medallion.
access_note: Do not download book. Use reviews, interviews, legal excerpts, or library access.

group_title: Quant Foundations - Renaissance / Simons / Medallion lineage
title: Public lectures and interviews on mathematics, science, and quantitative investing
why_it_matters: Useful context but not strategy disclosure. Treat as philosophy and culture, not reproducible trading logic.
abstract_summary: Public talks/interviews covering Simons' background, math, and broad views on quantitative investing.
access_note: Use official university/IAS/Numberphile pages where possible.

group_title: Quant Foundations - Renaissance / Simons / Medallion lineage
title: Optimal Gambling Systems for Favorable Games
venue: Review of the International Statistical Institute
why_it_matters: Historical bridge from gambling edge to systematic finance. Relevant to sizing, information advantage, and expected-value thinking.
abstract_summary: Develops optimal betting/gambling systems under favorable expected value.
access_note: Institutional access likely required; author/archive sources may exist.

group_title: Quant Foundations - Renaissance / Simons / Medallion lineage
title: The Kelly Criterion in Blackjack, Sports Betting, and the Stock Market
why_it_matters: Important for capital allocation under edge. Relevant to position sizing and risk-of-ruin controls in trading systems.
abstract_summary: Applies Kelly sizing concepts across gambling and financial-market settings.

group_title: Quant Foundations - Renaissance / Simons / Medallion lineage
title: Coding theory, game theory, and combinatorial mathematics papers relevant to Axcom/Renaissance predecessor culture
why_it_matters: Renaissance-specific trading details are non-public. Berlekamp's public work is relevant more for mathematical culture than market strategy.
abstract_summary: Public mathematical work by figures associated with early quantitative trading culture.

group_title: Quant Foundations - Renaissance / Simons / Medallion lineage
title: Commentary on quant investing and Renaissance-style statistical trading
why_it_matters: Useful external framing of what made Renaissance unusual: data discipline, scale, and validation. Not a substitute for technical market microstructure literature.
abstract_summary: Commentary/interviews on quantitative-investment evolution and statistical trading.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
title: The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis: Market Efficiency from an Evolutionary Perspective
why_it_matters: Core conceptual framework for regime adaptation. It gives a better mental model than static efficient-market or permanent-alpha thinking.
abstract_summary: Proposes adaptive markets as an evolutionary alternative to static market efficiency.
access_note: JPM/PM Research access likely required; search SSRN/author PDF.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
title: Adaptive Markets: Financial Evolution at the Speed of Thought
why_it_matters: Accessible expansion of AMH. Good for a founder building adaptive trading systems because it emphasizes competition, ecology, and changing opportunity sets.
abstract_summary: Book-length presentation of adaptive markets and financial evolution.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
title: The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis: Mathematical Foundations
why_it_matters: Mathematical formalization of AMH. Useful when turning the framework into testable regime/adaptation models.
abstract_summary: Develops mathematical foundations for adaptive markets.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
title: The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios
why_it_matters: Mandatory for evaluating strategy performance. Sharpe ratios without sampling-error awareness are a trap.
abstract_summary: Analyzes sampling distribution and inference for Sharpe ratios.
access_note: FAJ/Taylor access likely required; author versions may exist.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
authors: Andrew W. Lo, A. Craig MacKinlay
title: Stock Market Prices Do Not Follow Random Walks: Evidence from a Simple Specification Test
why_it_matters: Classic empirical challenge to random-walk assumptions. Useful background for technical-pattern and predictability claims.
abstract_summary: Tests random-walk behavior using variance-ratio style specification tests.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
authors: Mila Getmansky, Andrew W. Lo, Igor Makarov
title: An Econometric Model of Serial Correlation and Illiquidity in Hedge Fund Returns
why_it_matters: Important for hedge-fund return analysis. Smooth returns and illiquidity can fake performance stability.
abstract_summary: Models serial correlation and illiquidity effects in hedge fund returns.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
title: On the Evolution of Cryptocurrency Market Efficiency
why_it_matters: Shows AMH-style testing in crypto. Useful for regime-specific market-efficiency analysis.
abstract_summary: Tests adaptive market efficiency in cryptocurrency markets.

group_title: Andrew Lo / MIT Lab for Financial Engineering
title: A Test of the Adaptive Market Hypothesis using a Time-Varying AR Model in Japan
why_it_matters: Example of testing AMH with time-varying predictability. Useful for building simple regime-drift diagnostics.
abstract_summary: Uses time-varying autoregression to test adaptive market behavior in Japan.

authors: Shihao Gu, Bryan Kelly, Dacheng Xiu
title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
why_it_matters: Load-bearing ML asset-pricing paper. It benchmarks modern ML methods on expected returns and makes the cross-section problem concrete.
abstract_summary: Compares machine-learning methods for empirical asset pricing and return prediction.
access_note: Journal version paywalled; working-paper/preprint versions widely available.

authors: Bryan Kelly, Seth Pruitt, Yinan Su
title: Characteristics Are Covariances: A Unified Model of Risk and Return
why_it_matters: IPCA foundation. It explains how characteristics can represent conditional factor exposures, not just naive predictors.
abstract_summary: Builds an instrumented principal-components model linking characteristics to covariances and returns.
access_note: Elsevier access; author preprint likely available.

title: Machine Learning in Asset Pricing
why_it_matters: Compact theoretical guide to the ML asset-pricing frontier. Useful for separating prediction tools from pricing/economics.
abstract_summary: Book treatment of machine learning methods in asset-pricing research.

authors: Luyang Chen, Markus Pelger, Jason Zhu
title: Deep Learning in Asset Pricing
why_it_matters: Core deep-learning asset-pricing paper. It is a stronger baseline than generic LSTM trading demos.
abstract_summary: Uses deep learning to estimate stochastic discount factors and expected returns.

authors: Bryan T. Kelly, Boris Kuznetsov, Semyon Malamud, Teng Andrea Xu
title: Artificial Intelligence Asset Pricing Models
why_it_matters: Cross-listed from Group A because it is also the frontier AI asset-pricing anchor.
abstract_summary: Applies transformer-based AI models to stochastic discount factor estimation.

authors: Matthew Dixon, Nicholas G. Polson, Maria Goicoechea
title: Deep Partial Least Squares for Conditional Asset Pricing
why_it_matters: Useful method paper for high-dimensional conditional pricing. Relevant when feature space is large but economic interpretation matters.
abstract_summary: Combines partial least squares ideas with deep learning for conditional asset pricing.

title: Deep Learning for Conditional Asset Pricing Models
why_it_matters: Recent conditional asset-pricing work. Use as frontier scan, not a primary foundation until authors/version are verified.
abstract_summary: Applies deep-learning methods to conditional asset-pricing models.

title: The Impact of Uncertainty in Machine Learning Predictions on Asset Pricing
why_it_matters: Useful because uncertainty estimates matter for sizing and risk, not just point forecasts.
abstract_summary: Studies how predictive uncertainty from ML models affects asset-pricing conclusions.

title: The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities
why_it_matters: Foundational option-pricing paper. Required background for every volatility and options model.
abstract_summary: Introduces the Black-Scholes option-pricing framework.
access_note: JSTOR/Chicago access; many legal reprints exist.

title: Theory of Rational Option Pricing
venue: Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science
why_it_matters: Complements Black-Scholes with a broader continuous-time pricing framework. Required for stochastic calculus in finance.
abstract_summary: Develops rational option pricing in a continuous-time setting.

title: A Closed-Form Solution for Options with Stochastic Volatility with Applications to Bond and Currency Options
why_it_matters: Stochastic-volatility anchor. Most practical volatility modeling still references Heston-style dynamics.
abstract_summary: Presents a closed-form stochastic-volatility option-pricing model.

title: Pricing with a Smile
why_it_matters: Local-volatility foundation. Essential for understanding implied-volatility surfaces beyond Black-Scholes.
abstract_summary: Introduces local-volatility modeling from observed option smiles.

title: Option Valuation Using the Fast Fourier Transform
why_it_matters: Important numerical method paper. FFT pricing is useful when characteristic functions are known.
abstract_summary: Uses Fourier-transform methods for efficient option valuation.

title: The Volatility Surface: A Practitioner's Guide
why_it_matters: Practical volatility-surface reference. More useful for implementation than purely theoretical option papers.
abstract_summary: Book on implied-volatility surfaces, skew, term structure, and models.

title: Stochastic Volatility Modeling
why_it_matters: Deep practitioner reference for modern stochastic volatility. Useful for options desk-level modeling.
abstract_summary: Book on stochastic-volatility modeling and derivatives pricing.

authors: Christian Bayer, Peter Friz, Jim Gatheral
title: Pricing under Rough Volatility
why_it_matters: Rough volatility anchor. Important for understanding why volatility is not well captured by smooth diffusion assumptions.
abstract_summary: Develops option-pricing methods under rough volatility dynamics.
access_note: Find official arXiv/author PDF before download.

authors: D. Lemmens, L. Z. Cheng, S. Wang, A. L. Baaquie
title: A Path Integral Approach to Option Pricing with Stochastic Volatility
why_it_matters: Useful as alternative mathematical machinery for option pricing. Not core for a trading startup unless modeling derivatives directly.
abstract_summary: Applies path-integral methods to stochastic-volatility option pricing.

title: Option Pricing with Stochastic Volatility, Equity Premium, and Interest Rates
why_it_matters: Recent option-pricing scan. Useful for understanding models that combine volatility, equity risk premia, and rates.
abstract_summary: Studies option-pricing models incorporating stochastic volatility, equity premium, and interest rates.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
authors: Alexander J. McNeil, Rudiger Frey, Paul Embrechts
title: Quantitative Risk Management: Concepts, Techniques and Tools
why_it_matters: Risk modeling foundation. Use it before deploying any strategy with leverage, fat tails, or correlated drawdown risk.
abstract_summary: Textbook on statistical risk modeling, extreme values, dependence, and portfolio risk.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
title: Advances in Financial Machine Learning
why_it_matters: Practical ML-for-trading anchor. Useful for labeling, purging, embargoing, and backtest hygiene.
abstract_summary: Book on financial ML workflows, features, labeling, validation, and bet sizing.
access_note: Book purchase/library access; author papers are separately indexed.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
title: Machine Learning for Asset Managers
why_it_matters: Shorter applied guide than AFML. Useful for portfolio-oriented ML rather than pure signal hunting.
abstract_summary: Book on machine-learning tools for asset managers and portfolio construction.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
authors: David H. Bailey, Jonathan M. Borwein, Marcos Lopez de Prado, Qiji Jim Zhu
title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
why_it_matters: Mandatory. It explains why searching many strategies until one looks good produces fake alpha.
abstract_summary: Quantifies the probability that backtest selection produces overfit strategies.
access_note: Find official SSRN PDF when available.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
authors: David H. Bailey, Marcos Lopez de Prado
title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
why_it_matters: Mandatory performance-statistics paper. It gives a more realistic hurdle for strategy evaluation after multiple trials.
abstract_summary: Adjusts Sharpe-ratio inference for selection bias, non-normality, and multiple testing.
access_note: JPM version paywalled; SSRN working paper often available.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
authors: Campbell R. Harvey, Yan Liu, Heqing Zhu
title: ... and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
why_it_matters: Required for factor research. It shows why the factor zoo needs higher statistical thresholds.
abstract_summary: Studies multiple-testing problems in the cross-section of expected returns.
access_note: OUP access likely required; author preprint may exist.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
title: Empirical Properties of Asset Returns: Stylized Facts and Statistical Issues
why_it_matters: Core distributional facts: fat tails, volatility clustering, scaling, and non-normality. Use it before any model assumes Gaussian returns.
abstract_summary: Surveys stylized empirical facts of asset-return distributions.
access_note: Prefer author/institutional PDF over ResearchGate if found.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
authors: Peter Carr, Marcos Lopez de Prado
title: Determining Optimal Trading Rules without Backtesting
why_it_matters: Important because it attacks the usual backtest-mining loop. Useful for strategy design that starts from optimal stopping/control rather than brute-force search.
abstract_summary: Derives trading rules using analytical methods instead of traditional backtest selection.

group_title: Risk, Probability, Statistical Modeling for Trading
title: Revisiting the Stylized Facts of Financial Time Series
why_it_matters: Recent audit of classic stylized facts. Useful because market microstructure and electronic trading may alter old empirical regularities.
abstract_summary: Revisits empirical stylized facts of financial time series using modern data.

group_title: Volume, Order Flow, and ICT-style Microstructure - Academic Filter
authors: David Easley, Nicholas M. Kiefer, Maureen O'Hara, Joseph B. Paperman
title: Liquidity, Information, and Infrequently Traded Stocks
why_it_matters: Information-based trading anchor. Useful for understanding probability of informed trading and liquidity effects.
abstract_summary: Studies how information and liquidity affect infrequently traded stocks.

group_title: Volume, Order Flow, and ICT-style Microstructure - Academic Filter
authors: David Easley, Marcos Lopez de Prado, Maureen O'Hara
title: Flow Toxicity and Liquidity in a High-Frequency World
venue: Review of Financial Studies / Journal of Finance family
why_it_matters: VPIN/flow toxicity is one of the few rigorous academic ideas adjacent to retail order-flow concepts. Use carefully; it is debated.
abstract_summary: Studies order-flow toxicity and liquidity risk in high-frequency markets.
access_note: Institutional access likely required; preprints may exist.

group_title: Volume, Order Flow, and ICT-style Microstructure - Academic Filter
authors: Rama Cont, Arseniy Kukanov, Sasha Stoikov
title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
why_it_matters: Cross-listed because it is the academic version of order-flow imbalance. This is the paper to read before ICT-style claims.
abstract_summary: Quantifies how different order-book events contribute to price impact.

group_title: Volume, Order Flow, and ICT-style Microstructure - Academic Filter
title: Empirical Market Microstructure
why_it_matters: Best empirical reference for trades/quotes/spreads. Use it to define real microstructure features.
abstract_summary: Textbook on empirical market microstructure data and econometrics.

group_title: Volume, Order Flow, and ICT-style Microstructure - Academic Filter
title: Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
why_it_matters: Foundational informed-trading model. It explains price impact and strategic order submission from first principles.
abstract_summary: Models continuous auctions with strategic informed trading and market-maker price setting.

group_title: Volume, Order Flow, and ICT-style Microstructure - Academic Filter
authors: Lawrence R. Glosten, Paul R. Milgrom
title: Bid, Ask and Transaction Prices in a Specialist Market with Heterogeneously Informed Traders
why_it_matters: Bid-ask/information-asymmetry foundation. Useful for understanding why spreads exist and how adverse selection enters quotes.
abstract_summary: Develops a model of bid-ask spreads under asymmetric information.

group_title: Volume, Order Flow, and ICT-style Microstructure - Academic Filter
authors: ICT / Smart Money Concepts literature scan
title: Fair Value Gaps and Smart-Money Concepts: Academic Evidence Check
why_it_matters: Most ICT/fair-value-gap material is retail education, not peer-reviewed evidence. Treat it as hypothesis-generation only, then test with order-flow and microstructure features.
abstract_summary: No high-quality academic anchor found for retail ICT-style fair value gaps as a standalone edge.

authors: Andrew W. Lo, Harry Mamaysky, Jiang Wang
title: Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation
why_it_matters: The legitimate academic anchor for chart patterns. It converts vague visual patterns into algorithms and statistical tests.
abstract_summary: Develops computational/statistical methods for evaluating technical-analysis patterns.
access_note: Wiley access likely required; author PDF may exist.

authors: William Brock, Josef Lakonishok, Blake LeBaron
title: Simple Technical Trading Rules and the Stochastic Properties of Stock Returns
why_it_matters: Classic technical-rule evidence paper. It is a better baseline than social-media indicator claims.
abstract_summary: Tests moving-average and trading-range-break rules against stock-return null models.

title: What Do We Know About the Profitability of Technical Analysis?
why_it_matters: Survey anchor. Useful for quickly separating markets/time periods where technical rules showed evidence from those where they did not.
abstract_summary: Reviews empirical literature on technical-analysis profitability.
access_note: Wiley access likely required; author preprint may exist.

authors: Ryan Sullivan, Allan Timmermann, Halbert White
title: Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap
why_it_matters: Mandatory control paper for technical strategies. If a rule survives only because you searched thousands of variants, it is not alpha.
abstract_summary: Uses bootstrap methods to evaluate data-snooping bias in technical trading-rule performance.

authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse H. Pedersen
title: Time Series Momentum
why_it_matters: Institutional-grade trend-following anchor. More rigorous than indicator folklore.
abstract_summary: Studies persistent time-series momentum across asset classes.
access_note: Elsevier access; author/AQR preprint often available.

authors: Christopher J. Neely, Paul Weller, Rob Dittmar
title: Is Technical Analysis in the Foreign Exchange Market Profitable?
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
why_it_matters: Important FX technical-analysis evidence. Useful for separating market-specific effects from generic TA claims.
abstract_summary: Tests technical-analysis rules in foreign-exchange markets.

title: Pattern Recognition in Micro-Trading Behaviors before Stock Price Jumps
why_it_matters: Useful because it moves pattern recognition into micro-trading behavior rather than subjective chart labels.
abstract_summary: Studies patterns in micro-level trading behavior before price jumps.

title: Long Short-Term Memory Pattern Recognition in Currency Trading: Identifying Wyckoff Accumulation and Distribution Phases
why_it_matters: Interesting but lower-anchor quality. Treat as an example of trying to operationalize discretionary pattern concepts with sequence models.
abstract_summary: Uses LSTM-style pattern recognition for currency-trading phases inspired by Wyckoff concepts.

title: Prediction Markets
why_it_matters: Foundational prediction-market overview. Useful for thinking about markets as forecasting systems.
abstract_summary: Surveys prediction-market mechanisms, evidence, and applications.
access_note: JEP articles are often free; verify PDF from AEA.

title: Combinatorial Information Market Design
why_it_matters: Core mechanism-design background. Useful for market-scoring-rule and prediction-market product design.
abstract_summary: Develops mechanisms for information markets with combinatorial event structures.

title: Logarithmic Market Scoring Rules for Modular Combinatorial Information Aggregation
why_it_matters: The LMSR mechanism is central for automated market makers in prediction markets. Important if building forecasting systems with AI agents.
abstract_summary: Presents logarithmic market scoring rules for information aggregation.

title: Interpreting the Predictions of Prediction Markets
why_it_matters: Important caution: market prices are not automatically equal to true probabilities under all assumptions.
abstract_summary: Analyzes how prediction-market prices should be interpreted.

title: Risk Aversion, Beliefs, and Prediction Market Equilibrium
why_it_matters: Useful because trader risk preferences distort prediction-market prices. Relevant to AI-forecasting markets too.
abstract_summary: Studies how risk aversion and beliefs shape prediction-market equilibrium prices.

title: Fake Prediction Markets, Real Confidence Signals
why_it_matters: Recent AI/prediction-market frontier paper. Useful for separating market format from the confidence signal extracted from participants.
abstract_summary: Studies whether simulated/fake prediction markets can still reveal confidence signals.

title: Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Effects of Investor Beliefs and Strategies on Kalshi and Polymarket
why_it_matters: Current and directly relevant to real prediction markets. Useful for comparing belief aggregation versus strategy effects.
abstract_summary: Analyzes crowd wisdom in Kalshi and Polymarket using trader beliefs and strategies.

title: Prediction Arena: A Benchmark for LLM Forecasting over Prediction Markets
why_it_matters: Useful benchmark reference for LLM forecasting. It ties AI forecasting to market-like evaluation.
abstract_summary: Benchmarks LLM forecasting performance on prediction-market-style tasks.

title: LiveTradeBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Real-Time Financial Forecasting and Trading
why_it_matters: Important because static benchmark results are weaker than real-time forecasting. Useful for live evaluation harness design.
abstract_summary: Benchmarks LLMs on real-time financial forecasting and trading tasks.

title: Risks and Portfolio Decisions Involving Hedge Funds
why_it_matters: Hedge-fund risk foundation. Useful before trying to infer alpha from reported returns or holdings.
abstract_summary: Studies risk exposures and portfolio decisions involving hedge funds.

title: The Risk in Hedge Fund Strategies: Theory and Evidence from Trend Followers
why_it_matters: Hedge-fund factor anchor. Shows how hedge-fund returns can be decomposed into systematic exposures.
abstract_summary: Develops factor/risk explanations for hedge-fund strategy returns.

title: Hedge Fund Benchmarks: A Risk-Based Approach
why_it_matters: Important for benchmarking hedge fund performance. Prevents confusing beta-like exposures with manager skill.
abstract_summary: Builds risk-based hedge-fund benchmarks.

authors: Vikas Agarwal, Naveen D. Daniel, Narayan Y. Naik
title: Role of Managerial Incentives and Discretion in Hedge Fund Performance
why_it_matters: Useful for interpreting hedge-fund behavior through incentives. Incentives can drive risk-taking and reporting behavior.
abstract_summary: Studies how manager incentives and discretion affect hedge-fund performance.

authors: Vikas Agarwal, Wei Jiang, Yuehua Tang, Baozhong Yang
title: Uncovering Hedge Fund Skill from the Portfolio Holdings They Hide
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to holdings-based inference. It shows that omitted/hidden holdings can contain skill information.
abstract_summary: Uses confidential holdings data to infer hedge-fund skill from positions not publicly disclosed.
access_note: OUP access likely required; author preprint may exist.

title: Hedge Funds and the Technology Bubble
why_it_matters: Useful for understanding rational trading in bubbles. Hedge funds can ride mispricing rather than immediately arbitrage it away.
abstract_summary: Studies hedge-fund behavior during the technology bubble.

title: Do Hedge Funds Strategically Misreport Their Holdings?
why_it_matters: Important warning for 13F-based inference: reported holdings may not be a clean behavioral trace.
abstract_summary: Studies whether hedge funds strategically misreport or manipulate holdings disclosures.
access_note: Verify current paper page and authors.

authors: Miguel Anton, Lauren Cohen, Christopher Polk
title: Best Ideas
why_it_matters: Cross-listed because it extracts conviction from holdings. Useful input feature for 13F-based alpha models.
abstract_summary: Examines whether managers' concentrated positions represent highest-conviction ideas.

authors: Daniel Angelini, Hamish Iqbal, Farouk Jivraj
title: Systematic 13F Hedge Fund Alpha
why_it_matters: Cross-listed applied paper for 13F strategy design. Use as a practical benchmark.
abstract_summary: Tests systematic alpha extraction from 13F holdings.

title: X-Ray Machine Reveals About Hedge Funds
why_it_matters: Industry report that may be useful for holdings/risk decomposition. Lower priority than peer-reviewed work but potentially practical.
abstract_summary: Industry analysis of hedge-fund exposures/holdings through an X-ray style lens.
access_note: Verify exact report title/year and public availability.

group_title: Pattern Recognition in Markets / Macro-Micro AI Models
title: Pattern Recognition in Micro-Trading Behaviors before Stock Price Jumps
why_it_matters: Best fit for rigorous pattern recognition at micro level. It focuses on observable behavior before jumps rather than discretionary chart annotation.

why_it_matters: Useful for agent-based market simulation. It links trader learning behavior to emergent market dynamics such as volatility clustering.

group_title: Pattern Recognition in Markets / Macro-Micro AI Models
title: An Agent-Based Model for Designing a Financial Market that Works Well
why_it_matters: Useful for connecting micro decision rules to market-level outcomes. Relevant for simulation-first quant research.
abstract_summary: Uses agent-based modeling to study financial-market design and dynamics.

title: Empirical Properties of Asset Returns: Stylized Facts and Statistical Issues
why_it_matters: Cross-listed because pattern models need to reproduce real stylized facts. Without fat tails and volatility clustering, the simulator is fake.

title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
why_it_matters: Cross-listed because high-level pattern recognition becomes credible only when tested against strong ML asset-pricing baselines.

authors: Andrew W. Lo, Harry Mamaysky, Jiang Wang
title: Foundations of Technical Analysis
why_it_matters: Cross-listed as the academic pattern-recognition anchor for technical analysis.

authors: William A. Brock, Cars H. Hommes
title: Heterogeneous Beliefs and Routes to Chaos in a Simple Asset Pricing Model

authors: W. Brian Arthur, John H. Holland, Blake LeBaron, Richard Palmer, Paul Tayler
title: Asset Pricing under Endogenous Expectations in an Artificial Stock Market
why_it_matters: Classic artificial stock market. Useful for learning how micro rules produce macro market phenomena.

title: The Economy Needs Agent-Based Modelling
why_it_matters: Macro/micro modeling manifesto. Useful for thinking beyond equilibrium models and toward simulation-based economic systems.

title: Long Short-Term Memory Pattern Recognition in Currency Trading
why_it_matters: Lower priority example of applying sequence models to classical pattern language. Use only as a sandbox idea, not as evidence of robust edge.
